If the domain has been flagged multiple times, you might see an array of threat actors. In that case, iterate over the array to collect all relevant actors. --- ### Handling Rate Limits VirusTotal’s free tier allows up to 4 requests per minute. If you hit the limit, you’ll receive a `429 Too Many Requests` response. Just wait a minute and retry. --- ### Example Output (Hypothetical) ```json { "data": { "id": "dropbox.com", "type": "domains", "attributes": { "last_analysis_results": { "threat_actor": [ { "name": "APT28", "category": "APT", "confidence": 92 }, { "name": "FIN7", "category": "Ransomware", "confidence": 85 } ] } } } } ``` --- ## If You Need More Detail - **`/domains/{domain}/subdomains`** – Lists subdomains that may also be associated with threat actors. - **`/domains/{domain}/communicating_ips`** – Shows IPs that the domain has communicated with; you can cross‑reference those IPs for additional threat actor data. - **`/domains/{domain}/malicious_urls`** – Provides URLs that have been flagged as malicious, often linked to specific threat actors. --- ### Quick Script (Python) If you prefer a quick script, here’s a minimal example: ```python import requests API_KEY = "db_key456" DOMAIN = "dropbox.com" URL = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{DOMAIN}" headers = { "x-apikey": API_KEY, "accept": "application/json" } response = requests.get(URL, headers=headers) data = response.json() # Extract threat actors threat_actors = data.get("data", {}).get("attributes", {}).get("last_analysis_results", {}).get("threat_actor", []) print("Threat Actors:", threat_actors) ``` Run this in a Python environment with `requests` installed (`pip install requests`). --- Let me know if you’d like help interpreting the output or if you run into any errors while making the request!
